column3: NASB names “Ish-bosheth” for “the son of Saul”; “his hands dropped” is rendered “he lost courage.”
NASB supplies “had,” and opens a parenthesis that runs to the end of verse 3.
“Sojourners” is rendered “aliens”; NASB closes the parenthesis begun in verse 2.
“Stricken of feet” is rendered “crippled in his feet.”
“Lying the lying of noon” is rendered “taking his midday rest.”
The Hebrew reads “they came … taking wheat”; NASB renders “as if to get wheat.” The Hebrew is difficult.
“Removed his head” is rendered “beheaded him,” and “chamber of his lying down” as “bedroom.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “thus.”
“He was like a bearer of news in his own eyes” is rendered “thought he was bringing good news,” and NASB adds “which was the reward I gave him for his news.”
